evidence.claim: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent international validation of disclosure practices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: strong institutional transparency evidence, but not a direct measure of household welfare.
contrary_evidence: The same decision says beneficial ownership and some newer standards were not yet fully implemented.

evidence.claim: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent validation report with a concrete quantitative gap.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is about extractive-sector transparency under the incumbent government.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some progress in open-format disclosure.

evidence.claim: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
evidence.title: I Will Take My Percentage: Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
evidence.excerpt: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary investigative reporting with direct recording-based allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the conduct was tied to a close presidential adviser invoking access to Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The recording appears to be an apparent sting operation, so the evidentiary chain should be kept explicit.

evidence.claim: HRW said an activist died after denouncing embezzlement of mining royalties and that police violently dispersed an opposition sit-in over the election law, injuring and arresting protesters.
evidence.title: Child Labor and Human Rights Violations in the Mining Industry of the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: HRW said an activist died after denouncing embezzlement of mining royalties and that police violently dispersed an opposition sit-in over the election law, injuring and arresting protesters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous human-rights testimony with specific incident detail.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period evidence on corruption and coercive response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the incidents are attributed to state actors under the incumbent administration.
contrary_evidence: The report also shows the government remained under domestic and international pressure to reform.

evidence.claim: A covert-recording investigation showed Vidiye Tshimanga, one of Tshisekedi's closest advisers, offering to help investors win mining licenses and cut red tape in exchange for a stake, while describing ways to hide his share through proxies and offshore trusts.
evidence.title: "I Will Take My Percentage": Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
evidence.excerpt: A covert-recording investigation showed Vidiye Tshimanga, one of Tshisekedi's closest advisers, offering to help investors win mining licenses and cut red tape in exchange for a stake, while describing ways to hide his share through proxies and offshore trusts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The claim is supported by direct recordings, named participants, and in-article confirmation that the meetings occurred.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target period and tied to Tshisekedi's inner-circle network.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the conduct is by a close presidential adviser using proximity to Tshisekedi and claiming access through him.
contrary_evidence: Tshimanga denied wrongdoing and said the statements were taken out of context
the video-makers were unidentified

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Tshimanga resigned after being caught on tape negotiating a corrupt mineral deal, and that Tshisekedi's communications director said the fight against corruption is one of the president's pillars and that anyone in the Office of the President who violated the law would suffer the consequences.
evidence.title: Top Congo presidential adviser resigns after allegedly requesting bribe on tape
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Tshimanga resigned after being caught on tape negotiating a corrupt mineral deal, and that Tshisekedi's communications director said the fight against corruption is one of the president's pillars and that anyone in the Office of the President who violated the law would suffer the consequences.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous wire reporting with a direct presidency response and no dependence on a single anonymous source family.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to the president's office response; the underlying misconduct is by a close adviser in Tshisekedi's cabinet.
contrary_evidence: Tshimanga denied wrongdoing
the statement did not name Tshimanga

evidence.claim: The Kinshasa-Gombe prosecutor opened a judicial inquiry into former special adviser Vidiye Tshimanga and asked him to answer questions after the corruption allegations aired publicly in September 2022.
evidence.title: RDC : ouverture d'une information judiciaire à l'encontre de Vidiye Tshimanga
evidence.excerpt: The Kinshasa-Gombe prosecutor opened a judicial inquiry into former special adviser Vidiye Tshimanga and asked him to answer questions after the corruption allegations aired publicly in September 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local outlet reporting a formal prosecutorial step in direct response to the recorded allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong on the office network: the inquiry targeted a former special adviser to Tshisekedi, not an abstract national corruption climate.
contrary_evidence: The article reports allegations before final judgment
Tshimanga denied the accusations

evidence.claim: Ebuteli argued that Tshisekedi's September 2022 public-enterprise appointments kept a patronage pattern alive, with managers often chosen for party membership or family/friend ties and some appointees lacking sector experience.
evidence.title: Que retenir de la nomination des nouveaux mandataires publics en RDC ?
evidence.excerpt: Ebuteli argued that Tshisekedi's September 2022 public-enterprise appointments kept a patronage pattern alive, with managers often chosen for party membership or family/friend ties and some appointees lacking sector experience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Congolese research analysis that ties the appointments to a named ruling coalition and to specific selection criteria concerns, while remaining interpretive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Tshisekedi's appointment power and coalition-management choices.
contrary_evidence: This is an analytic podcast, not an audit of every appointee
the article frames some of the critique as inference about intent

evidence.claim: The State Department reported that in June Tshisekedi dismissed several Supreme Audit Court magistrates for failing to pursue corruption cases and appointed new leadership, then swore in 57 magistrates in August; it also said the APLC operated under the Office of the President.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The State Department reported that in June Tshisekedi dismissed several Supreme Audit Court magistrates for failing to pursue corruption cases and appointed new leadership, then swore in 57 magistrates in August; it also said the APLC operated under the Office of the President.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. government country report with specific, dated institutional actions and clear attribution to Tshisekedi.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Tshisekedi's authority over key accountability institutions.
contrary_evidence: The same report says the audit court rarely published its findings
it also says the APLC record was mixed

evidence.claim: The APLC said its Kolwezi team seized 33 trucks loaded with minerals and helped recover roughly 300 million dollars in fiscal revenue during the first half of 2022.
evidence.title: RDC : l'APLC annonce avoir saisi une trentaine de camions des minerais et permis le recouvrement fiscal de plusieurs millions de USD dans le Lualaba au premier semestre 2022
evidence.excerpt: The APLC said its Kolwezi team seized 33 trucks loaded with minerals and helped recover roughly 300 million dollars in fiscal revenue during the first half of 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific operational claim from the presidential anti-corruption agency, but still self-reported and not independently audited in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: the APLC is a presidential anti-corruption service operating under Tshisekedi's office.
contrary_evidence: The figure is self-reported by the APLC
the article does not independently verify the recovered amount

evidence.claim: At a Council of Ministers meeting, Tshisekedi urged the government to recover state real estate held or acquired unlawfully by third parties and to tighten controls on any disposition of state property.
evidence.title: RDC : Félix Tshisekedi encourage le gouvernement à récupérer le patrimoine immobilier de l’État acquis indûment par des tiers
evidence.excerpt: At a Council of Ministers meeting, Tshisekedi urged the government to recover state real estate held or acquired unlawfully by third parties and to tighten controls on any disposition of state property.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting on a direct presidential instruction affecting public assets and anti-spoliation controls.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the instruction is attributed to Tshisekedi in his executive role.
contrary_evidence: The source reports an instruction, not implementation
no independent recovery audit is provided here

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi appointed Jimmy Munganga Ngwaka to lead the Court of Accounts, which the article describes as an independent external controller of state finances and public entities.
evidence.title: RDC : Félix Tshisekedi nomme Jimmy Munganga Ngwaka, comme premier président de la cour des comptes
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi appointed Jimmy Munganga Ngwaka to lead the Court of Accounts, which the article describes as an independent external controller of state finances and public entities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear appointment notice with a direct description of the oversight role, though the independence claim is the article's framing rather than an observed outcome.
contrary_evidence: The appointment alone does not prove the court's later independence in practice
the source is a secondary summary of the ordinance

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
